title: Shader Alchemy: Robot's Enchanted Pool Arena
description: A robot stands at the edge of a mystical pool where chess pieces from ABeautifulGame float on a reflective water surface rendered with custom shaders. The user manipulates shader parameters to control water caustics, dissolve effects on the chess pieces, holographic projection on the robot, and a dynamic force field barrier between them — all through an interactive control panel requiring multi-step parameter tuning.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads three GLB assets: ABeautifulGame.glb (chess set), robot.glb, and pool.glb. Position the pool model at the scene center. Place the robot scaled appropriately standing beside the pool edge. Scatter 4-6 chess pieces from ABeautifulGame across the pool surface, floating with a gentle sine-wave bob animation. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,5,8) looking at origin. Add ambient light (0.3) and a directional light from (5,10,5). Implement these custom ShaderMaterial effects: 1) WATER SHADER on a plane inside the pool — animated caustic pattern using layered sine waves with uniform uTime, uCausticScale (0.5-5.0), and uCausticIntensity (0.0-1.0). 2) DISSOLVE SHADER applied to chess pieces — noise-based dissolve controlled by uniform uDissolveThreshold (0.0-1.0) with a glowing edge color uEdgeColor (color picker). 3) HOLOGRAM SHADER on the robot — scanline effect with uniforms uScanSpeed (0.1-3.0), uHoloColor (color picker), and uGlitchIntensity (0.0-1.0). 4) FORCE FIELD SHADER on a transparent sphere between robot and pool — Fresnel-based glow with uFieldStrength (0.0-2.0) and uFieldColor (color picker). Build a dat.GUI or HTML control panel with folders for each shader exposing all listed uniforms. Validate all numeric parameters stay within their defined ranges by clamping. The interaction flow requires: adjusting caustic scale and intensity (steps 1-2), tuning dissolve threshold and edge color on chess pieces (steps 3-4), configuring hologram scanline speed and glitch on the robot (steps 5-6), setting force field strength and color (steps 7-8). Use requestAnimationFrame to update uTime each frame. All shaders must use proper GLSL with vertex and fragment shaders defined inline. Add OrbitControls for camera navigation.
